newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI WINS CLEVELAND GP CART RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI WINS CLEVELAND GP CART RACE.

text.p: Italy's Alessandro Zanardi overcame two penalties which had dropped him to 22nd place to win the Cleveland Grand Prix CART race on Sunday.

Zanardi, driving a Reynard Honda, averaged 111.848 mph (179.996 kph). He took the lead with six laps remaining and finished ahead of Brazilian Gil de Ferran, also in a Reynard Honda, by 1.281 seconds. American Bryan Herta was third, in a Reynard Ford.
"I cannot do anything better than I did today," said Zanardi, celebrating his second win of the year and fifth of his career. "I didn't have anything left in my pocket.
Although he had the dominant, pole-winning car, a problem with his two-way radio could have cost him the victory.
When the right rear tyre of Richie Hearn's Lola exploded, causing him to spin and bringing out the first caution flag on lap 22, the leaders lined up in preparation for stops for fuel and tyres.

"I lost radio communication on the second lap," Zanardi explained. "Chip (Ganassi, his car owner) was screaming. The first thing I heard was 'Stay out, stay out.' The second thing I heard was 'Pit, pit.'"
Zanardi, then the race leader, was penalised for entering the pits, even though there was an official holding a red sign indicating the pits were closed.
"I didn't saee the sign whether the pits were opened or closed," the ITalian said.
Then when he exited the pits he violated a blend-line rule, merging too quickly into race traffic.

For the first violation, Zanardi was dropped to the back of the end of the line of the lead lap. Then when racing resumed, he was required to drive through the pits at less than 60 mph (97 kph) and he dropped to 22nd place.
Meanwhile de Ferran, who won here last year and qualified second, dominated the race but started to run low on methanol fuel.
"I was trying to drive for mileage," said de Ferran. "With ten laps to go I started losing my brakes. He (Zanardi) was trying hand over fist. I could not resist his attacks."

Paul Tracy of Canada, who finished seventh in a Penske Mercedes-Benz, continued to lead the series points standings with 106. Fellow Canadian Greg Moore was second with 95 and de Ferran third with 94.
The series moves to Toronto on July 20 for the 11th round of the 17-race series.
